summary:
The voting feature matches the design. I read every changed file whole except two that I read in part (see unreviewed). Those are: migration 0003, internal/votes, auth.Participant, POST /reports/{slug}/vote, the reader and admin composition, both templates, site.css, and the new or changed tests.

What I ran:
- `go vet ./...` and `go test -count=1 ./...` with HBAND_TEST_BROWSER set to Chrome. All packages pass.
- The E-003 finish-line test. I read its body from the ledger in place (epics id 41, SELECT only) and ran it from scratch against this worktree. Result: 1 test, OK, 5.2 s.
- Mutations in a scratch copy:
  - A dislike count added to PublicView and drawn only for the owner turns TestDislikesDoNotInterfere red on the owner's /, /reports/x and /reports/y. This confirms O-016.
  - Removing the kind CHECK from 0003 leaves the store, votes and server suites green. Nothing pins that constraint, and the migration test's row that claims to pin it passes for a different reason.
  - Changing the vote handler's report-lookup error from 503 to 404 leaves the server suite green.

Contract reads:
- Participant's three outcomes map one-to-one onto 503, a 303 that writes nothing, and a write.
- ErrNotOpen is returned only when the INSERT…SELECT finds no published row.
- Every non-error answer is the same 303, to the stored slug plus '#votes'. Slugs are [a-z0-9-], so LocalPath always accepts it.
- PublicView has no dislike field.
- OwnerTally has one caller, admin.go. Its error answers 500.

The facts the finish-line test relies on match the builder's account, (a) to (d).

The one major finding is outside the slice's lines. internal/testutil/headless.Browser falls back to msedge.exe when HBAND_TEST_BROWSER is unset. So `go test ./...` and case 14's check command start Edge on this machine. A repro is attached and I confirmed it fails.

Disclosure: one of my own runs started Edge. It was a full `go test ./internal/server/` in the scratch copy, for the lookup-error mutation. PowerShell environment variables do not carry between tool calls, so HBAND_TEST_BROWSER was unset, and TestReportScriptsNeverRun most likely started headless Edge once, with the harness's fresh profile. No headless msedge process was left running afterwards; I checked the process list.

The other findings are minor: an untested CHECK, an untested error branch, Withdraw not re-checking the report's status, and one stale comment.

Second reader, for inputs: I reviewed the inputs only and read every changed file whole: vote.go, votes.go, session.go, reader.go, router.go, admin.go, both templates, 0003_votes.sql, site.css, all new and changed tests, and the fitness.yaml and rule_spellings.json diffs.

I ran 23 crafted requests through the real handler chain (securityHeaders → CrossOriginProtection → Identify → mux) with a `go test -overlay` probe, so the worktree was not touched. Every outcome was sound:
- **Slug spellings:** a percent-escaped slug (/reports/%78/vote) is cast and the 303 is built from the stored slug. An upper-case slug, an escaped draft slug and an encoded slash all get the same `http.NotFound`.
- **Content types:** a charset parameter and an upper-case media type are accepted. Multipart, JSON and text/plain get 400.
- **Body shapes:** an escaped value (vote=%64own) and stray `&` are accepted. A BOM-prefixed key, a CR/LF or tab in the value, and a `;` in the body or the query string all get 400. A key that differs only in case is ignored.
- **Size cap:** a chunked body over 1 KiB with no Content-Length gets 400; one under 1 KiB is taken. An anonymous POST with a 10 MiB body gets 303 without the body being read.
- **Origin checks:** `Origin: null` gets 403. `Sec-Fetch-Site: none` and an Origin equal to the Host are let through by net/http's documented rules.

The time gap between looking up the report and writing the vote is closed for Cast, because the published check is inside the same statement. Withdraw is a plain DELETE, as designed. The rest of the input surface held:
- Slugs are limited to [a-z0-9-]{1,80} at upload, so the form action, the iframe src and the Location built from the stored slug cannot be steered.
- Every new fitness rule held on the tree. The local corpus passes and Fitness op=check passes 21/21. Following #939 I did not chase spelling variants past the named bounded_by.

I ran the full suite `go test -count=1 ./...` with HBAND_TEST_BROWSER set to Chrome and every package passed. No browser process was left running.

One defect, confirmed by running it: with HBAND_TEST_BROWSER unset, `headless.Browser` picks Microsoft Edge. That is the environment's empty case for the browser setting, and it means this slice's case-14 check (TestReportScriptsNeverRun), and the project's whole suite command, start Edge on this machine by default. The builder did exactly that on its first run. The code predates this slice (SL-003), but the engine classes a test that starts Edge by default as a defect to report, and this slice's matrix depends on that test.

findings.claim: internal/testutil/headless.Browser falls back to Microsoft Edge whenever HBAND_TEST_BROWSER is unset. So the project's whole-suite command `go test -count=1 ./...`, and case 14's check command `go test -count=1 -run '^TestReportScriptsNeverRun$' ./internal/server/`, start msedge.exe on this machine. The engine has measured Edge as not to be started here: at its first run it signs the profile in to the Windows Microsoft account and imports the person's old IE/Edge Legacy history. That has now happened on two runs: the builder's first full suite and one of this review's mutation runs. This slice depends on that test as its case-14 oracle, so every engine run of the case can start Edge. The project's decided testing stack says 'otherwise the default Edge path is used'. That decision predates the measurement and is outranked by it.
findings.evidence: headless.go:37-41 lists only the two msedge.exe paths. Browser (headless.go:49-64) returns the first one that exists when the variable is empty. On this machine it returned C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe (repro output).

quote.text:
// defaultBrowsers are where Edge installs on Windows.
var defaultBrowsers = []string{

findings.fix: Remove the Edge paths from defaultBrowsers. Either make the unset case skip with its message, or default to another Chromium-family browser such as the installed Chrome. Update the doc comment on Browser to match.

findings.claim: TestVotesMigrationOnAnExistingDatabase claims to pin 'kind is up or down', but its row {1, 8, "sideways"} uses github_id 8. That user was never inserted; only 7 signed in. The insert therefore fails on the users foreign key, not on CHECK (kind IN ('up','down')). In a scratch copy I removed the CHECK from 0003_votes.sql, and `go test ./internal/store/ ./internal/votes/` plus the server vote and reader tests all stayed green. Nothing in the tree pins the kind constraint: TestCastRefusesUnknownKind refuses before any SQL runs.
findings.evidence: internal/store/votes_migration_test.go:60-69. Only user 7 is created, at line 28. Mutation: CHECK removed, all three packages ok.
findings.fix: Use the existing reader and report in that row: {1, 7, "sideways"} on a fresh report, or delete the valid (1,7) row first. Then the CHECK is the only thing that can refuse it.

findings.claim: The vote handler has a branch where the report lookup fails with an error other than ErrNotFound. The design says it is logged and answers 503. No test reaches that branch. TestVoteIdentityUnavailable's closed-store subtest always fails at the identity step first, because it sends a grammar-valid sid, and its anonymous control runs with the library still working. In a scratch copy I replaced that 503 with http.NotFound, and `go test ./internal/server/` stayed green. A regression that turned a store outage into a 404, which would make every report look deleted, would go unnoticed. The case matrix names only the identity and votes-read failures.

quote.text: slog.Error("vote: look up the report", "error", err)

findings.fix: Add a TestVoteIdentityUnavailable subtest. Close the store, then POST with no session cookie, so Identify does no lookup. Assert 503, no Location, and Cache-Control no-store.

findings.claim: The handler looks up the published report and then writes. Cast re-checks status='published' inside its single statement. Withdraw does not re-check: it runs an unconditional DELETE. If the owner unpublishes the report between PublishedBySlug and the write, vote=none deletes the reader's vote from what is now a draft and answers 303. The contract says 404 for 'a report unpublished between lookup and write'. That changes the vote count the author sees on the draft. The design says drafts keep their votes and shows them on the admin page. The window is the gap between two statements, so the consequence is small.
findings.evidence: internal/votes/votes.go:78-84 (Withdraw) against Cast's `WHERE id = ? AND status = 'published'` at votes.go:60; vote.go:75-76 maps none to Withdraw with no ErrNotOpen path

quote.text: `DELETE FROM votes WHERE report_id = ? AND github_id = ?`

findings.fix: Add `AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reports WHERE id = ? AND status = 'published')` to Withdraw's DELETE. Alternatively, record in the contract that a withdrawal racing an unpublish is accepted.

findings.claim: The router comment calls the vote route 'The one public write'. POST /auth/logout, registered by a.auth.Routes(mux) at handlers.go:22, is also a write that any non-owner can reach. The comment misstates how many public write routes there are. That count matters to the noninterference route list (O-015) and to the waived ViewerFrom fence (N-029).

quote.text: The one public write: a signed-in reader sets their vote.

findings.fix: Change the comment to say this is the public write a reader uses to vote. Logout is the other public POST.

findings.claim: When HBAND_TEST_BROWSER is unset, Browser falls back to the Edge install paths in defaultBrowsers and returns C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe on this machine (measured). So TestReportScriptsNeverRun starts Edge every time the case-14 check (`go test -count=1 -run '^TestReportScriptsNeverRun$' ./internal/server/`) or the project's whole-suite command `go test -count=1 ./...` runs without the variable. The engine forbids starting Edge here: a new Edge profile is signed in to the Windows Microsoft account and silently imports the person's old browsing history. The builder's first full run of this slice did exactly that. The variable's unset value is the input the code gets wrong.
findings.evidence: headless.go:37-41 lists only the two msedge.exe paths as defaultBrowsers. Browser (lines 49-64) returns the first of them that exists when os.Getenv("HBAND_TEST_BROWSER") == "". The doc comment at lines 13-16 states the same. Running my repro through an overlay failed with: 'HBAND_TEST_BROWSER unset, and Browser chose Edge by default: C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe'. The build's own record says 'TestReportScriptsNeverRun used the default Edge for that one run'.
findings.fix: Take the msedge.exe entries out of defaultBrowsers. Either list only other Chromium-family install paths (for example C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe and its (x86) twin), or leave the list empty so an unset HBAND_TEST_BROWSER always skips. Change the doc comment (lines 13-16) and the skip message (line 62, which suggests msedge.exe) to match.

obligations.evidence: internal/votes/votes_test.go:83-108 TestCastSameVoteTwice casts Up three times and Down twice; one row, 1 like, then 1 dislike. Passes in my run.
votes_test.go:111-144 TestCastSwitches: up→down gives {0,1}, Mine down; down→up gives {1,0}; one row
votes_test.go:148-178 TestWithdrawWithoutVote: withdraw before any vote, twice after a vote, and on a missing report; all nil, the other reader's like kept
votes_test.go:182-217 TestVotesScopedPerReaderAndReport: two readers on report a give 2 likes; reader 7 on a and z counts once each; 4 rows

internal/server/vote_test.go:131-174 TestVoteAnonymousRefused: no session, expired (clock +31 d), unknown and malformed cookies get 303 to /reports/x#votes with no body and no rows. The anonymous / and /reports/x pages have no '/vote' and no name="vote", but do have 'Sign in to vote.' and '0 likes'.

vote_test.go:176-209: a valid reader sid with Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site or same-site, or Origin https://evil.example alone, gets 403 and 0 rows; same-origin and trusted-Origin controls get 303. Route registered inside cop at router.go:66,94.

vote_test.go:211-242: drafty, taken-down, deleted, unknown, UPPER-CASE and 81-character slugs, for anonymous, reader and owner, with 5 bodies each, all match the unknown-slug 404. reader_test.go:605-613 adds GET/HEAD/PUT 405 Allow POST, trailing slash 404, // 307, and draft x equal to unknown x.

vote_test.go:244-301 TestVoteBadFormRefused: missing, repeated, unknown, query-only, JSON, text/plain, 1025-byte and 64 KiB bodies all get 400 and write no rows; exactly 1024 bytes is accepted; the body value wins over the query string

vote_test.go:303-349: sessions table dropped gives 503 for live and unknown sids, the kept vote is unchanged, and anonymous still gets 303; store closed gives 503. vote_test.go:351-389: votes table dropped gives the 503 page on / and /reports/x for anonymous, reader and owner, with no like or form.
votes_test.go:237-265 TestCastRefusesUnpublished: a draft id, missing id 9999, and a report unpublished after a vote each give ErrNotOpen and change nothing

vote_test.go:391-456 TestVotesFollowReportLifecycle through the real admin routes: replace keeps the id and the votes; unpublish gives 404 and keeps both rows; republish; delete gives 0 rows; a new report under the same slug shows 0 likes

vote_test.go:458-613: the observers (anonymous, nonvoter, upvoter, and the owner's reader pages) over /, /reports/x, /reports/y, /reports, /admin, /admin/reports/x and their own vote POST stay byte-identical across 3+1 dislikes. A second world compares a switch with a withdrawal. Sensitivity controls cover the like change and the owner's tally going 0→3.

votes_test.go:336-413 TestConcurrentVotesNoBusy: 50 voters × 12 rounds of up/down/withdraw plus a final up, alongside 10 SignIn goroutines on store.Open's pool, 2 runs; any error is fatal; COUNT=50, Likes=50. Passes in my run (votes package 7.2 s).

browser_test.go:204-213 uploads 'blank' and shoots the anonymous /reports/blank, which now carries the votes section. site.css:12-14 uses only #8884 and inherited colours. It passed under Chrome in my full run. Its default browser is Edge; see M1.

Owed to validate-slice; this is my read only. observe() (vote_test.go:495) lists its routes by hand and leaves out GET /raw/{slug}, /healthz, /static/, /auth/github/* and POST /auth/logout. None of them references votes today: grep finds votes only in reader.go, admin.go, vote.go and router.go in the server package. So the claim to cover every route a non-owner can reach is literally false, but nothing leaks today, and m2 was deferred by decision.

vote_test.go:510-516 observes the owner's /, /reports/x and /reports/y, with an INVALID guard on the Admin link and 'Signed in as @the-owner'; the same sid is minted once at line 472. Mutation in a scratch copy: a Dislikes field on PublicView, drawn under {{if .Viewer.IsOwner}}, makes TestDislikesDoNotInterfere fail on all three owner pages.

Waived by the engine to note N-029; nothing was built, and .taad/fitness.yaml has no ViewerFrom rule. The waiver's premise holds: ViewerFrom is called only from internal/auth/owner.go, internal/server/reader.go:100 and admin.go:63, and the only public write handler, vote.go:29, uses auth.Participant.

It was waived, but built in substance. fitness.yaml rule 2's because text, and the bounded_by entry 'votes table SQL (SL-004 M-add-1)', name quoted and schema-qualified names and views or triggers created in later migrations. Corpus rows vote-sql-q004 (FROM \"votes\") and vote-sql-q005 (FROM main.votes) pin them as known-quiet.

fitness.yaml rule 3: `\.Begin(Tx)?\(`, `(?i)\b(BEGIN|SAVEPOINT)\b`, `\bsql\.Tx\b`. Rule 2 adds `\bUPDATE\s+OR\s+[A-Z]+\s+votes\b` and `\bFROM\b[^"`;]*,\s*votes\b`. Corpus fire rows vote-tx-f001..f007 (all at path internal/votes/votes.go) and vote-sql-f006..f009, plus quiet rows for 'begins', render(w, votes) and the known holes. The three bounded_by entries are present. TestRuleSpellingsCorpus passes.

I read the E-003 body read-only from the ledger (epics key E-003, project 14). (a) beside() scans every non-owner page for 2 or 3 next to a dislike label. (b) links[0] is the first 'sign in with github' anchor. (c) The test reads dislikes(owner, slug) from /admin/reports/<slug>. (d) The test posts vote=up|down|none to /reports/<slug>/vote; anonymous and forged posts need only answer below 500. Running it against this worktree: OK.

cases.evidence: votes_test.go TestCastSameVoteTwice really re-presses: Cast(Up) three times on a held up, Cast(Down) twice. RowsAffected=1 on conflict proved by no ErrNotOpen.
votes_test.go TestCastSwitches: holding up, sends Down; tally {0,1}, one row
votes_test.go TestWithdrawWithoutVote: withdraw with no vote ever cast, then twice after a vote
votes_test.go TestVotesScopedPerReaderAndReport: readers 7 and 8 on report a; reader 7 on a and z
vote_test.go TestVoteAnonymousRefused: no cookie, an expired session (clock advanced past 30 d), unknown and malformed cookies; the anonymous page is checked for no form
vote_test.go TestVoteCrossSiteRefused: a valid reader sid with Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site, and separately Origin https://evil.example with no Sec-Fetch-Site

TestVoteHiddenReportsAreIndistinguishable: draft, unpublished, deleted and unknown slugs, for anonymous, reader and owner. TestReaderPathVariants: GET, HEAD and PUT on the vote path, a trailing slash, //, and draft equal to unknown.
TestVoteBadFormRefused: missing, vote=up&vote=down, sideways, ?vote=up with an empty body, and bodies of 1025 bytes and 64 KiB
TestVoteIdentityUnavailable: sessions dropped and store closed, with a grammar-valid sid. TestReaderVotesReadFails: DROP TABLE votes, then GET / and /reports/x.
TestCastRefusesUnpublished: a draft id, missing id 9999, and a report set to draft after a vote
TestVotesFollowReportLifecycle: re-upload under the same slug, unpublish then publish, then delete, all through the real admin routes

TestDislikesDoNotInterfere: readers 20, 21 and 22 cast down on x (and 20 on y) between two observe() rounds that cover the listed routes and observers, including the owner's reader pages. Confirmed sensitive by my owner-gated leak mutation.
TestConcurrentVotesNoBusy: 50 goroutines cast, switch and withdraw, with 10 SignIn goroutines released from one channel, on store.Open's pool

browser_test.go:204-213: well 'blank-found' at the anonymous /reports/blank, which renders the votes section (like line and hint). It passed under Chrome. With HBAND_TEST_BROWSER unset it starts Edge (M1).

drift: The build account says no quiet rows were added for FROM "votes" and FROM main.votes (m4, waived to N-028). The tree has them: rule_spellings.json rows vote-sql-q004 and vote-sql-q005 pin exactly those spellings as known-quiet. The waived m4 work was built, and the account says it was not.
unreviewed: internal/fitnessrules/testdata/rule_spellings.json: read by parsing it with python -I json (lesson #945), not with Read. I listed every row, rules_under_test and the bounded_by entries for the three SL-004 rules. The other rules' rows were not read.
.taad/fitness.yaml: only the SL-004 hunk (lines 226-271) was read, through git diff 38e2b22..HEAD. The pre-existing rules above it were not re-read.
